default.notes: A visa is required for tourism (L visa). Apply at a Chinese embassy or visa application centre; the 240-hour visa-free transit is available when continuing to a third country through an eligible port.

groups.notes: Unilateral visa-free entry for up to 30 days (tourism, business, family visits, transit). Announced as valid through 31 December 2026 — confirm the scheme is still in force before travel.
Visa-free for up to 30 days under a mutual visa exemption agreement with China.
Visa-free under a mutual visa exemption agreement with China (up to 90 days in any 180-day period).
China opened trial visa-free entry (up to 30 days) from 1 June 2025, announced for one year initially and since extended. Trial policy — confirm it remains in force before travel.
Trial unilateral visa-free entry (up to 30 days) from 9 June 2025 — confirm it remains in force before travel.

CN.notes: Chinese citizens enter freely with a valid Chinese passport or ID travel document.

RU.notes: China opened trial visa-free entry for Russian citizens (up to 30 days, ordinary passports) from 15 September 2025, announced through 14 September 2026. Trial policy — confirm it remains in force before travel.

AZ.notes: Trial unilateral visa-free entry (up to 30 days) announced in 2025 — confirm it remains in force before travel.

MU.notes: Visa-free for up to 60 days under the China–Mauritius mutual visa exemption agreement.

HK.notes: Hong Kong residents enter the mainland using the Mainland Travel Permit (Home Return Permit) rather than the HKSAR passport.

MO.notes: Macao residents enter the mainland using the Mainland Travel Permit (Home Return Permit) rather than the Macao SAR passport.

TW.notes: Taiwan residents enter the mainland using the Taiwan Compatriot Travel Permit rather than the Taiwan passport; eligible travellers can obtain it in advance or at major ports of entry.
